speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your vertigo, specifically whether it feels like the room is spinning or if you feel lightheaded and unsteady?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in one ear during or after the episode? Also, do you have a history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or heart disease?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the spinning sensation last for several hours or days, or was it strictly a brief episode under one minute? Also, did you notice any weakness, numbness, or speech difficulties during the event?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Was the vertigo triggered by a specific change in head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up? I also need to know if you have any current hearing loss or tinnitus.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the brief duration and positional trigger, this sounds like BPPV, but I need to rule out central causes. I will now perform a physical examination to check for nystagmus and neurological deficits. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver
